questions.prompt:
Cobalt Bay Outfitters is adding four messaging channels to Dynamics 365 Contact Center. An administrator created each account in Copilot Service admin center, and each workstream is set up. The Facebook app, the LINE channel, the Teams app and the Azure bot resource already exist on the provider side, and the custom channel uses the Azure bot framework method.

Each account now shows connection details that have to reach the provider before customer messages can arrive.

You need to complete the provider side of each connection.

What should you do for each channel?

tokens.text: Add the callback URL and verify token to the app's webhook settings, then subscribe the page to Messages
Set the callback URL as the webhook URL in the Messaging API settings, turn on the webhook, and verify it
Enter the bot ID under App features in Developer Portal, then publish the app
Paste the messaging endpoint URL into the Messaging endpoint field of the bot resource
Copy the inbound URL from the workstream, and paste it into the Messaging section of the active phone number
Copy the callback URL, and paste it into the webhook field of a notification profile that uses HMAC authentication

rows.label: Facebook
LINE
Microsoft Teams
Custom channel

questions.answer: Facebook: Add the callback URL and verify token to the app's webhook settings, then subscribe the page to Messages. LINE: Set the callback URL as the webhook URL in the Messaging API settings, turn on the webhook, and verify it. Microsoft Teams: Enter the bot ID under App features in Developer Portal, then publish the app. Custom channel: Paste the messaging endpoint URL into the Messaging endpoint field of the bot resource.
questions.explanation: Every out-of-the-box channel ends the same way: handshake data has to be exchanged between the application and the provider. What changes is where it goes. Facebook uses the callback URL and verify token to configure the app's webhooks, and the page needs a subscription to Messages. LINE takes the callback URL as the webhook URL in the Messaging API settings, with the webhook toggle on and the connection verified. For Teams, the account's callback information gives a bot ID instead, which goes under App features in Developer Portal. A custom channel with the Azure bot framework method gives a messaging endpoint for the Azure bot resource. The other two steps belong to SMS providers: Twilio takes an inbound URL on the phone number, and Infobip takes the callback URL in a notification profile.

optionExplanations.a: Correct for Facebook. The callback URL and verify token configure the app's webhooks, and the page needs a subscription to Messages. LINE has no page subscription step.
optionExplanations.b: Correct for LINE. The copied callback URL becomes the webhook URL in the Messaging API settings, the webhook toggle is turned on, and the connection is verified.
optionExplanations.c: Correct for Microsoft Teams. The account's callback information gives a bot ID, which is entered under App features in Developer Portal before the app is published.
optionExplanations.d: Correct for the custom channel. The Messaging endpoint (URL) from the account goes in the Messaging endpoint field of the Azure bot resource.
optionExplanations.e: Fails on every row. This is the Twilio step, where the inbound URL goes in the Messaging section of an active SMS number. None of these four channels uses one.
optionExplanations.f: Fails on every row. This is the Infobip step, where the callback URL goes in a notification profile secured with HMAC. None of these four channels uses one.

questions.prompt:
Sundial Credit Union has three messaging projects on Dynamics 365 Contact Center. Its chat widget stays on the public website.

The mobile team will follow Microsoft's recommended approach for native apps. For this program, the security team doesn't allow any bot registration in Azure Bot Service.

You need to choose the integration surface for each project.

What should you use for each project?

tokens.text: Contact Center Messaging SDKs for iOS and Android
Live chat SDK for the chat widget
Custom messaging channel through Direct Line
Web chat widget inside a WebView

rows.label: New native member app with in-app messaging and push notifications
Back-end service that relays conversations from the in-house secure message center to representatives
Website code that shows the start-chat option only while the target queue is within operating hours

questions.answer: Native member app: Contact Center Messaging SDKs for iOS and Android. Back-end relay: Messaging APIs. Website code: Live chat SDK for the chat widget.
questions.explanation: Choose by where the code runs. For a native app, Microsoft strongly recommends the mobile SDKs, which include push notification support through Azure Notification Hub. Messaging APIs are built for service-to-service work and aren't recommended for calls from a user's device, so they fit the back-end relay and not the app. A custom channel through Direct Line could also bring in an in-house channel, but its documented setup needs a Bot Framework bot registered with Azure Bot Service, and security doesn't allow that here. On the website, the Live chat SDK method getAgentAvailability returns isQueueAvailable, and Microsoft names this method for deciding whether the start conversation option should be visible.

optionExplanations.a: Correct for the native app. Microsoft strongly recommends these SDKs, and they support push notifications with Azure Notification Hub. They're for native mobile apps, not for a back-end service or a website.
optionExplanations.b: Correct for the website code. The getAgentAvailability method of the Live chat SDK reports whether the queue is within operating hours.
optionExplanations.c: Correct for the back-end relay. Messaging APIs are designed for service-to-service integration and for custom channels. They aren't recommended for direct calls from a mobile or web client.
optionExplanations.d: Fails on every row. The documented custom channel setup needs a bot built with Bot Framework and registered with Azure Bot Service, which security doesn't allow here.
optionExplanations.e: Fails on every row. A WebView is the fallback when the mobile SDKs don't meet requirements or timelines, and it has reduced performance and unavailable features. The mobile team is following the recommended approach.

questions.prompt:
Larchmont Appliances runs its chat channel with Dynamics 365 Customer Service, so representatives work with cases. The chat widget has a pre-conversation survey with a required single-line question named Email. No other identification method is in use. All contacts have the standard active status, and no account holds these email addresses.

The team lead is writing a guide that shows what representatives see after they accept a chat.

You need to identify the result of each test.

What is the result of each test?

tokens.text: The contact and the case are linked to the conversation
The contact is linked, and no case is linked
No contact or case is linked
The most recently updated contact is linked to the conversation
A new contact is created and linked to the conversation

rows.label: Matches one contact, and that contact has one active case
Matches one contact, and that contact has three active cases
Matches two contacts

questions.answer: One contact with one active case: The contact and the case are linked to the conversation. One contact with three active cases: The contact is linked, and no case is linked. Two contacts: No contact or case is linked.
questions.explanation: Automatic identification links a record only when the result is a single record. A survey answer that matches one contact links that contact, and if the contact has one active case, that case is linked automatically too. Three active cases give no single case to link. An answer that matches two contacts links neither, because the application doesn't pick a record for you. The representative can still search for or create a record on the Active Conversation page.

optionExplanations.a: Correct for one contact with one active case. Microsoft says the case is linked automatically when the identified contact has one active case.
optionExplanations.b: Correct for one contact with three active cases. The contact is a single match, but the automatic case link applies when there's one active case.
optionExplanations.c: Correct for two contacts. When the search returns more than one contact, the record isn't linked to the conversation.
optionExplanations.d: Fails on every row. The application doesn't choose between matches. More than one result means the record isn't linked.
optionExplanations.e: Fails on every row. Identification searches existing records. Creating a record is something the representative does on the Active Conversation page.

questions.prompt:
Tansy Pet Supply is adding an SMS channel through Infobip in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. SMS for Infobip is provisioned. The messaging account in Copilot Service admin center holds the API base URL and an API key with the message:send scope, and the SMS workstream is set up.

An administrator is now finishing the Infobip portal. The SMS number is assigned to a new application. The SMS subscription uses the inbound message and delivery events and filters on that application, and the number's default inbound forwarding action is Apply subscription.

You need to finish the portal setup so that customer messages reach representatives.

What should you use for each item?

rows.label: Application ID of the new Infobip application

options.text: The organization ID of the Dynamics 365 environment
The environment ID of the Dynamics 365 environment
The application (client) ID of a Microsoft Entra app
The tenant ID of the Microsoft Entra tenant

rows.label: Secret key in the HMAC authentication settings

options.text: The API key entered in the messaging account
A second API key created only for webhooks
The verify token from the callback information

rows.label: Callback URL from the messaging account

options.text: The Webhook URL field of a notification profile
The Messaging section of the SMS number
The application filter of the SMS subscription settings

questions.answer: Application ID: The organization ID of the Dynamics 365 environment. HMAC secret key: The API key entered in the messaging account. Callback URL: The Webhook URL field of a notification profile.
questions.explanation: Infobip inbound delivery depends on three values that are easy to confuse. The Infobip application's ID has to be the Dynamics 365 organization ID, and Microsoft specifically says not to use the environment ID, tenant ID or Microsoft Entra application ID. The HMAC settings reuse the same API key that's in the messaging account, and a mismatch is one of the listed reasons that messages don't arrive. The callback URL goes in the Webhook URL field of a notification profile, which the subscription then uses.

optionExplanations.r1a: Correct. The Application ID is set to the organization ID, and the subscription's application filter then selects the application whose ID matches it.
optionExplanations.r1b: Fails. Microsoft says to use the organization ID, not the environment ID.
optionExplanations.r1c: Fails. Microsoft says to use the organization ID, not the Microsoft Entra application ID.
optionExplanations.r1d: Fails. Microsoft says to use the organization ID, not the tenant ID.
optionExplanations.r2a: Correct. The same API key that's in the messaging account is the secret key for HMAC authentication.
optionExplanations.r2b: Fails. The HMAC secret has to match the API key in the messaging account, and a mismatch is listed as a cause when messages don't arrive.
optionExplanations.r2c: Fails. A verify token is a Facebook value. The Infobip account's callback information gives a callback URL, and the secret key is the API key.
optionExplanations.r3a: Correct. The callback URL goes in the Webhook URL field of the notification profile, with the HMAC settings selected under Security settings.
optionExplanations.r3b: Fails. This is where the inbound URL goes for Twilio. For Infobip, the number's settings hold the application and the inbound forwarding action.
optionExplanations.r3c: Fails. The application filter selects the application whose ID matches the organization ID. It doesn't hold a URL.

questions.prompt:
Juniper Street Books connected its Facebook page to Dynamics 365 Contact Center through a Facebook app. The Provisioning state of the page shows Running, and the workstream and routing are configured.

A pilot found these gaps:
- Only people who have a role in the Facebook app can message the page.
- Representatives can't reply once 24 hours have passed since a customer's last message.

You need to close the gaps.

What should you do for each item?

rows.label: Let any customer message the page without being given a role in the Facebook app

options.text: Get the pages_messaging permission approved through Meta App Review
Refresh the page access token on the Facebook account
Turn on the Facebook message tag on the channel instance
Add the callback URL to the app again, and resubscribe the page to Messages

rows.label: Let representatives reply after the 24 hours have passed

options.text: Set Facebook message tag to Yes on the channel instance, and turn the tag on in the Facebook app
Set Facebook message tag to Yes on the channel instance, and leave the Facebook app unchanged
Turn the tag on in the Facebook app, and leave Facebook message tag set to No on the channel instance
Set Auto-close after inactivity to seven days on the workstream, and leave Facebook message tag set to No

questions.answer: Customers without a role: Get the pages_messaging permission approved through Meta App Review. Replies after 24 hours: Set Facebook message tag to Yes on the channel instance, and turn the tag on in the Facebook app.
questions.explanation: These are two separate limits. Who can message the page depends on the Facebook app. Until Meta approves pages_messaging through App Review, only people with a role in the app can message the page. How long representatives can reply depends on the Facebook message tag. With the tag set to No, representatives can't respond after 24 hours unless the customer sends another message. The tag has to be on in both places: the channel instance's User features and the Facebook app.

optionExplanations.r1a: Correct. Until Meta approves pages_messaging for the app, only Facebook users with a role in the app can message the page.
optionExplanations.r1b: Fails. Page access tokens need refreshing on a schedule, but the limit on who can message the page comes from the pages_messaging approval.
optionExplanations.r1c: Fails. The message tag controls how long representatives can reply. It doesn't change who can message the page.
optionExplanations.r1d: Fails. The callback URL and subscription connect the app to Dynamics 365. The limit here comes from the pages_messaging approval.
optionExplanations.r2a: Correct. Microsoft says the tag must also be turned on in the Facebook app, so both places are needed.
optionExplanations.r2b: Fails. Microsoft says that to use the human agent message tag, you must also turn it on in the Facebook app.
optionExplanations.r2c: Fails. With Facebook message tag set to No, representatives can't respond after 24 hours unless the customer sends another message.
optionExplanations.r2d: Fails. Auto-close after inactivity decides when inactive conversations close. The 24-hour reply limit depends on the message tag.

questions.prompt:
Alpine Ridge Travel has a custom customer portal that isn't built on Power Pages. Its web team is adding authenticated chat to the portal's chat widget in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. An authentication settings record will be added to the widget, and the portal will issue a signed JSON Web Token (JWT).

Requirements:
- Signing keys rotate. During each rotation, tokens signed with the old key and with the new key must both validate.
- A representative sees the signed-in customer's contact record, and the customer isn't asked any questions.
- The chat button appears on public pages, so a visitor can select it before signing in.

You need to design the token flow.

What should you do for each requirement?

rows.label: Key rotation

options.text: Return kid and public key pairs from the public key endpoint, and pass kid in the JWT header
Point the Public key URL in the authentication settings record at a new endpoint that returns only the new key
Keep one public key at the endpoint, and pass the new public key in the lwicontexts claim

rows.label: Contact record

options.text: Put the GUID of the contact record in the sub claim
Put the GUID of the contact record in the iss claim
Put the GUID of the contact record in the kid header

rows.label: Visitor who isn't signed in

options.text: Redirect the visitor to sign in from the JavaScript client function or an earlier step
Have the JavaScript client function return an expired token until the visitor has signed in
Add a pre-conversation survey question that asks visitors to enter an email address

questions.answer: Key rotation: Return kid and public key pairs from the public key endpoint, and pass kid in the JWT header. Contact record: Put the GUID of the contact record in the sub claim. Visitor who isn't signed in: Redirect the visitor to sign in from the JavaScript client function or an earlier step.
questions.explanation: A custom portal owns the token flow, so each requirement maps to a specific part of it. To use several public keys, the endpoint returns unique kid and public key pairs, and the JWT header carries the kid. To link the record, Microsoft recommends passing the contact or account GUID in the sub claim. The system uses it to identify and link the contact. A chat button that's visible before sign-in needs a redirect, either in the JavaScript function or earlier in the user flow, because an expired or invalid token makes the widget throw an error event.

optionExplanations.r1a: Correct. When multiple public keys are needed, the endpoint can return a set of kid and public key pairs, and the kid is passed in the JWT header.
optionExplanations.r1b: Fails. The system validates each token with the public key from the record's Public key URL. An endpoint that returns only the new key can't validate tokens signed with the old key during the rotation.
optionExplanations.r1c: Fails. lwicontexts carries context variables for routing or display. Public keys come from the public key endpoint.
optionExplanations.r2a: Correct. Microsoft recommends passing the GUID of the contact or account record in sub, which is used to identify and link the record.
optionExplanations.r2b: Fails. The iss claim holds the issuer of the token.
optionExplanations.r2c: Fails. The kid value identifies which public key signed the token.
optionExplanations.r3a: Correct. If the button is exposed before users are authenticated, Microsoft says to redirect them to your authentication page, in the JavaScript function or as an earlier step.
optionExplanations.r3b: Fails. If the token has expired or is invalid, the chat widget throws an error event.
optionExplanations.r3c: Fails. A survey answer can identify a record, but identification doesn't authenticate the customer. The requirement is for a signed-in chat.

questions.prompt:
Seaholm Cruises uses real-time translation for chat in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. It uses its own web resource, based on Microsoft's sample, with Azure Translation Services as the provider. Translation is turned on, the web resource URL is registered, and representatives work in English.

During testing, a customer writing in Portuguese sends one short message in English, and translation stops until the customer writes in Portuguese again. Separately, the Azure Translation Services resource is being set up for production, and a bilingual representative asks to read one customer's messages untranslated.

You need to configure the solution.

What should you do for each item?

rows.label: Keep translation running after a one-off message in another language

options.text: Set enableLanguageDetectionWithHistoryMessages to true in the web resource file
Set Default input language to Portuguese on the Real Time Translation Settings page
Turn translation back on with More commands in the chat window after each one-off message

rows.label: Endpoint for the Azure Translation Services resource

options.text: The global endpoint
A regional endpoint in the same geography as the environment
A private endpoint in the company virtual network

rows.label: Switch translation off for one conversation

options.text: The representative uses More commands in the chat window
An administrator sets Turn on to No in the Real Time Translation Settings
An administrator sets enableLanguageDetectionWithHistoryMessages to false

questions.answer: One-off message: Set enableLanguageDetectionWithHistoryMessages to true in the web resource file. Endpoint: The global endpoint. One conversation: The representative uses More commands in the chat window.
questions.explanation: With the web resource approach, each of these has its own place. Score-based language detection is a value in the web resource file. It moves translation to the most-used language, so a one-off message doesn't change or stop it. When Azure Translation Services is the provider, Microsoft says the resource must use the global endpoint. The switch for a single conversation belongs to the representative, through More commands in the chat window. The administrator's Turn on setting applies to the feature as a whole.

optionExplanations.r1a: Correct. Setting this value to true enables score-based language detection, which prevents one-off messages from changing the language unexpectedly.
optionExplanations.r1b: Fails. Default input language sets the language that representatives work in. Representatives here work in English.
optionExplanations.r1c: Fails. More commands turns translation on or off for one conversation. Turning it back on after each one-off message doesn't keep it running, and Microsoft's documented fix for one-off messages is score-based detection in the web resource file.
optionExplanations.r2a: Correct. Microsoft says that with Azure Translation Services as the provider, you must configure the resource to use the global endpoint.
optionExplanations.r2b: Fails. Microsoft says the resource must use the global endpoint.
optionExplanations.r2c: Fails. Microsoft says the resource must use the global endpoint.
optionExplanations.r3a: Correct. Representatives can turn translation on or off for each conversation by using More commands on the chat window.
optionExplanations.r3b: Fails. This is the setting that turns on the feature in the admin center, so it isn't a choice for one conversation.
optionExplanations.r3c: Fails. This value controls score-based language detection. It doesn't switch translation off.

questions.prompt:
Kestrel Telecom handles support through an SMS workstream and a live chat workstream in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. The live chat workstream doesn't use persistent chat. Representatives accept both types of conversation, so each conversation below starts in Active.

The operations lead is updating the representative guide.

You need to state the status reason that follows each event.

What is the status reason after each event?

rows.label: SMS: the representative selects the close (X) button and doesn't select End

options.text: Open
Waiting
Wrap-up
Closed

rows.label: Live chat: the representative selects the close (X) button and doesn't select End

options.text: Open
Waiting
Wrap-up
Closed

rows.label: Live chat: the customer's connection drops, and the customer stays away for longer than the reconnection duration

options.text: Open
Waiting
Wrap-up
Closed

questions.answer: SMS close without End: Waiting. Live chat close without End: Open. Live chat customer disconnection: Wrap-up.
questions.explanation: The same button has different results because live chat has no Waiting status. On an asynchronous channel, closing the session with X and not End moves the conversation to Waiting, which releases the representative's capacity until the customer comes back. On live chat, the same action sends the conversation to Open for reassignment. A live chat customer who stays disconnected past the set duration, three minutes by default, ends the exchange, so the application moves the active chat to Wrap-up and updates capacity.

optionExplanations.r1a: Fails. Open is the live chat and voice result. On asynchronous channels, this action leads to Waiting.
optionExplanations.r1b: Correct. On persistent chat and asynchronous channels, closing with X and not End moves the conversation to Waiting, and capacity is released at once.
optionExplanations.r1c: Fails. Wrap-up follows the End button. Here the representative didn't select End.
optionExplanations.r1d: Fails. An SMS conversation in Waiting closes later, through inactivity. It doesn't close at this event.
optionExplanations.r2a: Correct. On voice and chat, closing with X and not End sends the conversation to Open so that it can be reassigned.
optionExplanations.r2b: Fails. Waiting applies to asynchronous and persistent chats only, not to live chat.
optionExplanations.r2c: Fails. Wrap-up follows the End button or a customer ending or leaving the chat.
optionExplanations.r2d: Fails. The conversation is still in progress, so the system reassigns it.
optionExplanations.r3a: Fails. Open applies while the conversation is unassigned or being reassigned. An active chat that the customer leaves moves forward to Wrap-up.
optionExplanations.r3b: Fails. Waiting doesn't apply to live chat.
optionExplanations.r3c: Correct. When an ongoing chat gets disconnected, the application moves it from Active to Wrap-up and updates capacity.
optionExplanations.r3d: Fails. Closed is the result for a disconnection from Open. From Active, the chat moves to Wrap-up.

questions.prompt:
Harbor Cycle Insurance wants to add one more messaging channel to Dynamics 365 Contact Center for claims.

Requirements:
- Customers send documents, such as claim forms, to representatives during the conversation.
- An AI agent greets customers first and offers suggested actions that customers can select.

File attachments will be turned on for customers on the chosen channel, and any client work that the channel needs for attachments will be done.

You need to choose a channel that meets both requirements.

Which two channels meet both requirements? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Facebook
Custom messaging through Direct Line
LINE
WhatsApp through Twilio
Microsoft Teams

questions.answer: Facebook, and custom messaging through Direct Line.
questions.explanation: Check each requirement against the channel support tables separately, because neither one predicts the other. Inbound attachments are what matters for a form that a customer sends. Facebook and Teams list Document, custom messaging through Direct Line accepts all types except those blocked in the organization, LINE's inbound list has no Document, and WhatsApp through Twilio lists PDF. Teams and WhatsApp don't support suggested actions. Facebook, LINE and Direct Line support suggested actions. Only Facebook and Direct Line appear on both lists.

optionExplanations.a: Correct. Facebook lists documents for inbound attachments and supports suggested actions.
optionExplanations.b: Correct. Direct Line custom channels accept all inbound types except those blocked in the organization and support suggested actions. The client has to implement attachments, which the scenario covers.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. LINE supports suggested actions, but its inbound attachments are image, audio, video and GIF, with no Document.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. WhatsApp through Twilio doesn't support suggested actions.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. Teams accepts inbound documents, but it doesn't support suggested actions.

questions.prompt:
Fern Hollow Garden Centre has a modern chat widget on its website in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. From 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, customers must be able to start a chat. Outside those hours, customers must not see any way to start one.

Those hours are set up as operating hours on the chat queue. The workstream has no AI agent, the web team can change the website's code, and the site gets only a few visitors a minute.

You need to meet the requirement.

Which two solutions meet the requirement? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Turn on Show widget during operation hours, select the operating hour record, and leave Show widget outside of operation hours cleared.
Add data-hide-chat-button to the widget script. After lcw:ready, call getAgentAvailability, and show your own button, which calls startChat, only if isQueueAvailable is true.
Add data-hide-chat-button to the widget script. After lcw:ready, call getAgentAvailability, and show your own button, which calls startChat, only if isAgentAvailable is true.
Set the action for the chat queue's Out of operation hours overflow condition to End conversation, and edit its closing message.

questions.answer: Turn on Show widget during operation hours with the record and leave Show widget outside of operation hours cleared. Or hide the default button and show a custom button only when getAgentAvailability returns isQueueAvailable as true.
questions.explanation: The requirement is about what customers can see, so the solution has to act before a chat starts. The widget setting does this directly: the widget displays during the hours in the selected record, and it appears outside them only if the outside-hours option is selected. Code can do the same. The data-hide-chat-button tag removes the default button, and getAgentAvailability tells the page whether the queue is within operating hours, so a custom button can follow that result. isAgentAvailable follows representative availability, not operating hours, so a button built on it can disappear while the queue is open. Overflow acts only after a customer has started a conversation, so the way to start one stays visible.

optionExplanations.a: Correct. The widget displays during the hours in the selected record, and it displays outside them only if Show widget outside of operation hours is selected.
optionExplanations.b: Correct. The tag hides the default button, and isQueueAvailable is true when the queue is within operating hours, so the page can show a custom button only then. Microsoft names this method for deciding whether the start option is visible.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. isAgentAvailable is true when representatives in the queue are available to take requests, not when the queue is within operating hours. If no representative is available to take requests during opening hours, it's false and the button disappears, but customers must still be able to start a chat then.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. Overflow conditions for before a work item is queued run after the customer starts a conversation, and End conversation ends it then. The widget stays visible, so customers still see a way to start one.

questions.prompt:
Stonebridge Property Management uses unified routing in Dynamics 365 Customer Service. It wants each email sent to its support mailbox to reach representatives automatically as an email record.

The following are in place:
- Email is added on the Record routing page.
- The mailbox uses server-side synchronization to create the email record and queue item.
- A Record workstream for Email has classification and route-to-queue rules.
- Queues and assignment methods are set up.
- A process releases representative capacity when work on an email is done.

You need to finish the routing setup.

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Create an intake rule that maps incoming email records to the Email workstream.
Create a cloud flow that runs msdyn_ApplyRoutingRuleEntityRecord when an email row is created.
Create a route-to-queue rule that sends incoming email records to the Email workstream.
Set the Route Case field to Yes on the records that are created from the support mailbox.
Add the support mailbox to a Messaging workstream as an email channel instance.

questions.answer: Create an intake rule that maps incoming email records to the Email workstream, and create a cloud flow that runs msdyn_ApplyRoutingRuleEntityRecord when an email row is created.
questions.explanation: Microsoft documents a path for routing email as a record, and the two steps not yet done here are the flow and the intake rule. Server-side synchronization creates the record, but something has to trigger routing, and the documented flow runs msdyn_ApplyRoutingRuleEntityRecord when an Email Messages row is created. Intake rules then help determine which workstream receives the record. Route-to-queue rules work inside a workstream, so they can't choose it.

optionExplanations.a: Correct, and part of the solution. Intake rules help determine the workstream to use for an incoming record work item.
optionExplanations.b: Correct, and part of the solution. The documented custom flow triggers on a new Email Messages row and applies the routing rules to it.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. Route-to-queue rules belong to a workstream and send work items to its queues. Intake rules help determine which workstream receives the record.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. Route Case is a case field that decides whether a new case is routed. The records here are emails.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. Messaging workstreams route live chat, SMS, social and Teams conversations. Email is a record, so it uses a Record workstream.

questions.prompt:
Hillcrest Medical Supply handles orders over SMS in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. Representatives often ask a customer for a purchase order number, and the customer takes hours to reply. Meanwhile, the conversation holds the representative's capacity.

Managers want an active timeout rule on the SMS workstream so that after four hours:
- The representative can take other work while the customer is away.
- The representative is notified when the customer replies.

You need to configure the rule.

Which two settings should you use? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Trigger event: Customer Non-Response Time
Trigger event: Representative Non-Response Time
Action: Move active conversation to waiting
Action: Send a message
Action: Release conversation back to queue for reassignment

questions.answer: Trigger event: Customer Non-Response Time. Action: Move active conversation to waiting.
questions.explanation: The clock here starts with the representative's last message, which is what Customer Non-Response Time measures. The action decides what happens to the conversation. Moving it to Waiting fits, because a conversation in Waiting doesn't consume capacity, the option exists for asynchronous channels such as SMS, and the representative gets a notification when the customer restarts the conversation. Sending a message leaves the conversation in Active, where capacity is consumed. Releasing it frees capacity, but it reassigns the conversation to a different representative.

optionExplanations.a: Correct, and part of the solution. This trigger measures how long a customer stays inactive after the representative's last message.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. This trigger measures how long a representative leaves a customer's message unanswered, which is the opposite situation.
optionExplanations.c: Correct, and part of the solution. For asynchronous channels, this action moves the conversation to Waiting, and the representative is notified when the customer restarts it.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. This action sends a message and leaves the conversation in Active, where the representative's capacity is still consumed.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. This action reassigns the conversation to a different representative in the same queue, so it's no longer this representative's conversation when the customer replies.

questions.prompt:
Pinecrest Logistics runs a custom messaging channel through Messaging APIs in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. The channel instance is on a messaging workstream, and its queue often has a backlog.

While customers wait, they must get a message with their current place in the queue every five minutes until a representative is assigned.

You need to configure the message.

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: On the channel instance, add a custom message for the Estimate Wait Time Notification trigger, and include {QueuePosition} in the text.
In the custom message pane, set Message interval to 5 minutes, and turn on the isRecurring toggle.
On the Behaviors page of the channel instance, turn on Customer wait time, and select the option to show customers their position in the queue.
On the Automated messages page, activate the Average wait time for customers: Minutes message for the channel.
On the channel instance, add a custom message for the Customer's position in queue trigger, and include {$QueuePosition$} in the text.

questions.answer: Add a custom message for the Estimate Wait Time Notification trigger with {QueuePosition} in the text, and set Message interval to 5 minutes with isRecurring turned on.
questions.explanation: Messaging API channel instances have their own wait time notification. It's a custom automated message on the Estimate Wait Time Notification trigger, and the {QueuePosition} variable shows the customer's current place. Message interval sets how often it's sent, and isRecurring repeats it until a representative is assigned. The other routes look similar, but they can't meet the five-minute cycle. The Customer wait time setting sends updates on fixed intervals of 30 or 60 seconds, and the average wait time messages apply to live chat and voice. The {$...$} format is for context variables, so with no such variable it becomes an empty string.

optionExplanations.a: Correct, and part of the solution. This is the trigger for Messaging API channel instances, and {QueuePosition} shows the customer's current position.
optionExplanations.b: Correct, and part of the solution. Message interval sets the time between messages, and isRecurring repeats the message until a representative is assigned.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. Queue position notifications from this setting go at fixed intervals of 30 or 60 seconds, so it can't send one every five minutes.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. The average wait time messages apply to live chat and voice channels only, and they give a wait time and not a place in the queue.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. {$...$} is the context variable format, and a variable that isn't found becomes an empty string. Message interval and isRecurring are documented for the Estimate Wait Time Notification trigger.

questions.prompt:
Sorrel Lodge Hotels runs Dynamics 365 Contact Center standalone. Its booking portal has a chat widget that uses authenticated chat with a JSON Web Token (JWT). Proactive chat is turned on, and after lcw:ready the page calls startProactiveChat when a signed-in guest has spent 30 seconds on a booking.

The developer based the page on Microsoft's proactive chat samples, which call setContextProvider to send values. The booking reference and loyalty tier are sent this way, but they don't reach the conversation, although the workstream has context variables with the same names. The portal's token service already knows both values.

You need to send both values so that they can be used for routing and shown to the representative.

What should you do?

options.text: Add both values to the lwicontexts claim in the JWT payload.
Add both values to the JWT header beside the alg and typ values.
Call setContextProvider before the lcw:ready event is raised.
Set isDisplayable to true for both values in setContextProvider.
Add both values to the notificationUIConfig object for the invitation.

questions.answer: Add both values to the lwicontexts claim in the JWT payload.
questions.explanation: The samples for proactive chat use setContextProvider, but Microsoft notes that this method works for unauthenticated chat only. For authenticated chat, context travels in the JWT. The lwicontexts value in the payload holds serialized custom context, its keys must correspond to the workstream's context variables, and the values can be used for routing or shown to the representative. The widget's sign-in state decides the method, and proactive chat doesn't change that.

optionExplanations.a: Correct. Pass lwicontexts in the JWT payload for authenticated chat. Its keys must match the workstream's context variables, and it can carry values for routing or display.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. The JWT header holds values such as alg, typ and kid. Context variables go in the lwicontexts claim of the payload.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. SDK methods run after lcw:ready, and setContextProvider isn't supported for authenticated chat at any point.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. isDisplayable controls display of values that setContextProvider passes, and that method isn't supported for authenticated chat.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. notificationUIConfig customizes the invitation, including its message. It doesn't set context variables.

questions.prompt:
Mossgrove Foods uses a survey from Customer feedback as the post-conversation survey on live chat in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. The survey agent is published in Copilot Studio, and the survey is selected on the channel with Powered by Microsoft Copilot Studio.

A maker changed the rating question so that it stores the 1 to 5 score in a new variable named MCS_Rating. Responses appear in the Customer feedback survey response table, but the satisfaction scores for conversations don't appear in the Omnichannel historical analytics report.

You need the scores to appear in the report.

What should you do?

options.text: Store the score as a numeric value in the MCS_CSAT variable.
Pass the score in mcs_additionalcontext as a JSON key value pair.
Store the score as a text value in the MCS_CSAT variable.
Move the MCS_Rating question to a system topic other than Conversation Start.

questions.answer: Store the score as a numeric value in the MCS_CSAT variable.
questions.explanation: Two variable rules are at work. An added question's response is stored in Dataverse when its variable name starts with MCS_, which is why MCS_Rating appears in the response table. The report is more specific: scores for conversations appear in the Omnichannel historical analytics report if they're stored as numeric values in the MCS_CSAT variable. So the data was saved, but not in the variable that the report reads.

optionExplanations.a: Correct. Microsoft says scores for conversations appear in the Omnichannel historical analytics report if they're stored as numeric values in MCS_CSAT.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. mcs_additionalcontext passes extra context to the survey agent. It isn't where the report reads scores.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. Microsoft says scores for conversations appear in the Omnichannel historical analytics report if they're stored as numeric values in MCS_CSAT. A text value doesn't meet that condition.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. Conversation Start is the only system topic to edit. Microsoft says all other system topics are disabled and must not be used.

questions.prompt:
Brightwell Insurance has a French-language chat widget on its Quebec workstream in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. The compliance team approved a set of French quick replies. Each one has the French locale and is associated with the Quebec workstream. French is enabled in the environment.

When the Quebec representatives open quick replies, they're offered the English replies, and they have to choose French in the View all pane to find the approved text.

You need these representatives to be offered the French replies without that extra step.

What should you do?

options.text: Change the language in each representative's personal settings to French.
Remove the Quebec workstream association from the French quick replies.
Set Default input language to French in the Real Time Translation Settings.
Add a French tag to the approved quick replies.

questions.answer: Change the language in each representative's personal settings to French.
questions.explanation: Three things decide which quick replies a representative sees: the language mapped to the channel instance, the language in the representative's personal settings, and the workstream. The widget language and the workstream are already right. The remaining factor is the representative's own setting, because when it's configured, it determines the language in which quick replies are available. Tags and workstream associations change which replies can be found, not the language that's offered.

optionExplanations.a: Correct. When a representative has a language configured, that setting determines the language in which quick replies are available.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. With no association, a reply is available to all representatives, but the language setting still decides which language they're offered.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. Default input language is the language that translation uses for representatives. It doesn't decide which quick replies are offered.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. Tags group quick replies, and finding replies by tag is still an extra step for the representative.

evidence.section: Add a wait time notification for the Messaging API channel; Waiting in queue; Context variables
evidence.claim: For a Messaging API channel instance, the Estimate Wait Time Notification trigger takes a message, with {QueuePosition} for the customer's current position, a Message interval in minutes, and an isRecurring toggle that repeats the message until a representative is assigned. Average wait time messages apply to live chat and voice channels only. Context variables use {$Name$}, and a missing variable becomes an empty string.

evidence.section: Show customers their position in a queue
evidence.claim: The notification goes at an interval of every 30 seconds if the queue position is fewer than 150 items, and every 60 seconds above that. It's enabled with Customer wait time on the Behaviors tab.
evidence.applicability: Distractor c fails on the five-minute requirement, whatever the channel. Page dated 2025-11-27.

evidence.claim: To add another question and store the data in Dataverse, the response variable name must start with MCS_. evidence.section: Availability of quick replies and language settings; Associate quick replies with a workstream; Create or edit tags
evidence.claim: Three parameters determine the quick replies that representatives see: the language mapped to the channel instance, the language configured in the representative's personal settings, and the workstream. The representative-specific language setting, if configured, determines the language in which the quick replies are available. If no workstream is associated, the quick reply is available for all representatives. Tags classify quick replies.
evidence.applicability: All options. Page dated 2026-06-30.

evidence.section: Send quick replies
evidence.claim: In View all, representatives can choose a language and search for quick replies. Representatives can search by tag with /q.
evidence.applicability: Stem, which treats choosing a language in View all as the step to remove, and distractor d. Page dated 2026-10-26.

evidence.section: Languages tab options
evidence.claim: Personal settings has a Languages tab, and adding a language other than the base language needs the administrator to install and enable the language pack.
evidence.applicability: The stem states that French is enabled. The quick reply page calls this the language configured in personal settings, and the option uses those words. Page dated 2026-10-30.

evidence.section: Enable real-time translation for representative and customer conversations
evidence.claim: Default input language is the language for representatives to converse with customers, and translation renders customer messages in it.
evidence.applicability: Distractor c.
